result.title: I Think, Therefore I Attack: Evaluating Thought Injection Attacks on Reasoning Agents
result.summary: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) are one of the key components of current agentic systems. LRMs augment their output with an explicit chain-of-thought reasoning stage, introducing a new attack surface for thought injection, in which untrusted text resembling the model's own deliberation is fed back to the model. We present a two-part study of this attack, performed against the prevailing large, production class open-weight models (e.g., GLM-5.3, MiniMax-M2.5, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). We first evaluate the effectiveness of static thought-injection prompts under different styles as well as tagged and untagged conditions and find that the effects of thinking tags and payload styles are all properties of the specific target model. In the second study, we exploit this model-specificity in a containerized agentic cyber range, using indirect injection prompts styled in the form of the target model's own reasoning traces to achieve attack success rates (ASR) up to 50% on operational objectives such as reverse-shell exfiltration and repository backdooring. We also find that the same malicious objective in standard prompt injection user voice never succeeds, and thinking tags suppress the agent's tendency to disclose the injection. Our results show that imitating a reasoning model's own thought style is effective for this style of attack, and that tag stripping is an unreliable defense.

AI.brief_summary: 研究针对大型推理模型的「思维注入」攻击：先测试静态注入提示在不同风格及有无 thinking tag 条件下的效果，再在容器化智能体靶场中用模仿目标模型自身推理痕迹的间接注入，取得最高 50% 的攻击成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文显示模型会把伪装成自身思考的文本当作可信内部状态、且依赖标签的区分并不可靠，这可能可供核查 LVR 中内部推理状态与外部证据的边界、思考标记作为状态隔离手段的有效性及状态来源可信度，但材料本身无视觉或多模态推理内容。
